# Review code against production

Proofline reviews pull requests against the infrastructure they will deploy into, so you can find evidence-backed deployment risks, inspect the evidence, and see what remains unknown.

## Evidence behind each finding

Proofline connects your code change to a read-only snapshot of your cloud and checks the constraints between the change and that infrastructure. It then publishes supported findings in GitHub, along with the evidence behind each one.

## Your infrastructure stays under your control

Infrastructure integrations are read-only. You choose which repositories to connect and how to address the findings.

## FREE Code Reviews

Get one month of [free code review](https://proofline.sh/blog/free-ai-code-review) for private repositories, or free code review for public repositories.

review_comments.body:
**🟡 Medium · Exported reports become malformed**

When a report name contains a comma, quote, or newline, including a newline followed by a spreadsheet formula, `write_export` joins fields without CSV quoting or escaping, so delimiters split columns or records; an attacker can use the newline to create a formula cell that executes when an operator opens the export in a spreadsheet.

Serialize rows with a CSV writer and neutralize spreadsheet formula cells before writing.

review_comments.body:
**🟡 Medium · Exports block writes or remain truncated**

When a large export writes slowly while another process commits a database change, or the cursor raises after yielding rows, the lazy cursor remains active while output is written, holding a read lock that can make concurrent commits time out; if the cursor raises, the already-written header and rows remain as a truncated export.

Fetch all rows before writing the header or any output, so the cursor is closed before writing begins and a fetch error leaves no partial export.

Also at `reports.py:56`.
